stem: Pretransplant evaluation identifies untreated cryptococcosis in a solid-organ transplant candidate. Which management step aligns with standard infection references?

options.text: A minimum of 4 months of antifungal therapy such as fluconazole before transplant
No treatment because fungal disease never affects transplant candidacy
Immediate transplant without any antifungal therapy
Antifungal therapy limited to 48 hours only

explanation.rationale_correct: If cryptococcosis, coccidioidomycosis, or histoplasmosis are identified pretransplant, a minimum of 4 months of antifungal therapy is recommended with agents such as fluconazole.

rationale_incorrect.B: Pretransplant endemic fungal disease requires treatment before transplantation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Untreated cryptococcosis is not managed by proceeding immediately to transplant without therapy.
rationale_incorrect.D: Standard references recommend at least 4 months of antifungal therapy rather than brief treatment alone.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: cryptococcosis, coccidioidomycosis, or histoplasmosis are identified pretransplant, a minimum of 4 months of antifungal therapy is recommended with antifungal agents such as fluconazole

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 17 → fungal infections → pretransplant cryptococcosis/coccidioidomycosis/histoplasmosis (≥4 months fluconazole); PDF p. 943 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Pretransplant endemic-fungal therapy angle distinct from evaluation viral studies (cctc-2086) and PCP timing (cctc-3093); anchor verified on Cupples p. 943.

stem: When explaining how deceased-donor kidneys may travel farther for allocation, which technology aligns with standard kidney transplant references?

options.text: Increased use of perfusion devices allowing kidneys to remain outside the body longer
Elimination of all cold ischemia time requirements for every organ
Mandated same-hospital implantation for all kidneys regardless of logistics
Perfusion devices are used only for heart allocation, never kidneys

explanation.rationale_correct: With increased use of perfusion devices, kidneys can remain outside the body for longer periods, making it possible to allocate kidneys across greater distances than some other solid organs.

rationale_incorrect.B: Perfusion extends preservation time but does not eliminate ischemia considerations entirely.
rationale_incorrect.C: Greater geographic allocation is enabled by extended preservation rather than requiring same-site implantation only.
rationale_incorrect.D: Perfusion devices are described in kidney allocation context rather than being heart-only technology.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: increased use of perfusion devices, kidneys can remain outside of the body for longer periods of time … allocate kidneys across greater distances

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → Kidney transplantation → allocation → c.d. (perfusion devices and extended geographic allocation); PDF p. 49 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Kidney-perfusion allocation angle distinct from EPTS/KDPI (cctc-2097/2098) and cold-ischemia definition (cctc-2090); anchor verified on Cupples p. 49.

stem: A pretransplant candidate schedules a dental procedure. Which coordination step aligns with standard health-maintenance references?

options.text: Discuss the procedure with the transplant team at least a week before the appointment because dental prophylaxis may be required
Never inform the dentist of immunosuppressed status
Proceed with any dental surgery without transplant-team notification
Dental care is permanently contraindicated after listing

explanation.rationale_correct: Dental care includes informing the dentist of immunosuppressed status; dental prophylaxis may be required depending on the procedure, and the transplant team should be consulted at least a week before the appointment.

rationale_incorrect.B: Recipients should inform the dentist of immunosuppressed status.
rationale_incorrect.C: Certain dental procedures require transplant-team coordination and possible prophylaxis.
rationale_incorrect.D: Regular dental visits are recommended rather than permanent contraindication.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → health maintenance → Dental care
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Inform dentist of immunosuppressed status … Dental prophylaxis may be required … Discuss with transplant team at least a week before appointment

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → health maintenance → Dental care (inform dentist; team consult ≥1 week before procedures); PDF p. 118 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Pretransplant dental-coordination angle distinct from dentition screening (cctc-2051) and post-transplant dental teaching; anchor verified on Cupples p. 118.

stem: When coordinating pretransplant health-maintenance screening, at what age should the first colonoscopy screening examination be completed per standard references?

options.text: By age 50, or earlier when indicated by history
Only after 10 years post-transplant regardless of age
Colonoscopy is never recommended for transplant candidates
Only before age 18 for every candidate

explanation.rationale_correct: Colonoscopy screening includes completing the first screening examination by age 50 or as recommended for inflammatory bowel disease or family history of colon cancer.

rationale_incorrect.B: Colonoscopy screening is part of pretransplant health maintenance rather than deferred exclusively until 10 years post-transplant.
rationale_incorrect.C: Colonoscopy is listed among recommended health-maintenance screening studies.
rationale_incorrect.D: Age 50 is the standard first-screening reference rather than universal screening only before age 18.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → health maintenance → Colonoscopy
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Complete first screening examination by age 50 or as recommended for history of inflammatory bowel disease or family history of colon cancer

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → health maintenance → Colonoscopy (first screening by age 50 or earlier when indicated); PDF p. 118 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Colonoscopy age-50 screening angle distinct from bone densitometry (cctc-2052) and skin/dentition screening (cctc-2051); anchor verified on Cupples p. 118.
